My land is on the North China Plain, same as my father's land and his father's before him. I have farmed wheat and maize on this soil my whole life and I am not going to change that now at 78. My knees hurt, my son lives in the city, so I keep things simple. I rent out a few mu I cannot manage anymore, but I still work about 4 mu myself.

Winter wheat goes in the ground around October. I always use the improved variety seeds from the township supply station — the old varieties cannot compete anymore and everyone here uses the newer ones. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress with urea when the wheat joints in spring. I irrigate four times: once at sowing to get good germination, once before the ground freezes in winter, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray once for aphids and rust in late spring. The machine comes to harvest in June — I pay for that service.

Right after wheat harvest I plant summer maize on the same ground. Same 4 mu. Hybrid seed. I top-dress nitrogen once when the maize is knee-high. Rain is usually enough in summer but I irrigate once if it gets dry in August during grain fill. One pesticide spray for corn borer. Rotary tillage before planting maize because it is easier on my back than deep plowing, and it handles the wheat stubble well enough.

I expect maybe 450 jin of wheat per mu and around 550 jin of maize. Nothing fancy. Just enough to sell some grain and keep flour for the family.
